first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding is the current preference because it directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, while avoiding the margin and customer-quality risks of reacting immediately with discounts. Verify memory_86 for durability and downstream outcomes, and memory_73 to compare promotional pricing on qualified revenue, retention, and margin—not just acquisition lift. A guarded test is appropriate because neither summarized record establishes long-term qualified revenue conclusively.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly matches the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its +18% qualified-revenue lift was accompanied by 30-day retention falling 12% and failure through the first renewal cycle. Uncertainty remains about whether the earlier onboarding effect will replicate under current conditions, so experiment rather than broadly roll out.
